title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes and CKD stage 4.

HPI
The patient is a 73-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his chronic conditions. He has a long-term history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and has been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease stage 4. He reports consistent adherence to his current medication regimen. He denies any new acute symptoms or significant changes in his functional status since the last visit. He continues to monitor his glucose levels at home and reports they remain within his target range.

Medication List
- Insulin
- Glipizide
- Lisinopril

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Skin is warm and dry. Lung sounds are clear to auscultation. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current regimen.
2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4: Stable for this visit.

Plan
1. Continue current insulin and oral hypoglycemic medications.
2. Monitor renal function and continue follow-up as scheduled.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: CKD is listed under 'with' for diabetes in the Index, so the link is presumed: use the combination code E11.22.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: The provider does not have to write 'due to'; 'with' presumes the link.
E11.2 is a subcategory; a 5th character is required.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
